title.id: Peraturan Pengendalian Kasino (Kontrak yang Wajib Diberitahukan) 2026
title.ms: Peraturan Kawalan Kasino (Kontrak yang Wajib Dimaklumkan) 2026

completenessNote: 全文，共 12 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。附表 2 篇以 900000+ 序号随同收录。

text.en: 1. These Regulations are the Casino Control (Notifiable Contracts) Regulations 2026 and come into operation on 21 September 2026.

3. To avoid doubt, a contract for the purposes of Division 3 of Part 4 of the Act includes —
(a)any agreement or arrangement, whether with or without valuable consideration; and
(b)any agreement or arrangement between a person and a casino operator for the supply by another person (other than the first‑mentioned person) of goods or services to the casino operator.

4.—(1) In these Regulations, any reference to the value of a contract is a reference to —
(a)the total amount of money or money’s worth payable at the completion of the contract in respect of the performance of the contract —
(i)including any amount payable for goods or services which may be acquired by an option granted under the contract; but
(ii)excluding any goods and services tax (or equivalent tax) payable in relation to the supply of the goods or services under the contract; and
(b)where a number of distinct contracts are entered into in connection with the same casino operator —
(i)with the same vendor; and
(ii)within a continuous period of 12 months (including any period before 21 September 2026),
the aggregate value of all such contracts, each computed in accordance with sub‑paragraph (a).
(2) If the value of a contract or variation of a contract is denoted in foreign currency, in determining whether an amount of foreign currency is equivalent to a Singapore dollar amount under these Regulations, the amount of foreign currency is to be converted to Singapore currency at the exchange rate applicable at the time the contract or variation is entered into.
(3) Despite paragraph (1)(b), if, in the opinion of the Authority, any contract forms part of a series of contracts that may reasonably be considered to have been entered into with a view to evading the provisions of the Act and these Regulations in relation to notifiable contracts, the value of the contract is the total amount of money payable, in respect of the performance of such of the contracts in the series as the Authority may determine.
5. These Regulations apply to contracts entered into before, on or after 21 September 2026.

heading.en: Prescribed matter to which contract relates

text.en: 6. For the purposes of paragraph (a) of the definition of “notifiable contract” in section 72(1) of the Act, the matters specified in the First Schedule are prescribed matters.

7. For the purposes of paragraph (b) of the definition of “notifiable contract” in section 72(1) of the Act, the prescribed value is $500,000 or its equivalent in a foreign currency, computed in accordance with regulation 4, even if the value of any single contract does not exceed $500,000.

8.—(1) The prescribed classes of notifiable contracts in respect of which a casino operator must give the written notice required under section 74(1)(a) of the Act are set out in the first and second columns of Part 1 of the Second Schedule.
(2) The written notice must be given no later than the 20th day of the month immediately following the month in which a prescribed notifiable contract was entered into or varied, as the case may be.
(3) The written notice must provide —
(a)the particulars of the contract or variation, together with any supporting documents, in the form and manner specified by the Authority by prior written notice; and
(b)any other information or documents that the Authority may require in any particular case by prior written notice.

heading.en: Ongoing monitoring and disclosure requirements by casino operator

text.en:
9.—(1) Where a casino operator becomes aware of any occurrence or matter relating to a vendor or a notifiable contract that may be reasonably regarded as being likely to adversely affect the credibility, integrity and stability of its casino operations, the casino operator must consider whether to terminate —
(a)any or all contracts between the casino operator and the vendor (whether or not a notifiable contract); or
(b)the notifiable contract in question.
(2) Where the casino operator mentioned in paragraph (1) decides not to terminate any one or more of the contracts between the casino operator and the vendor or the notifiable contract, the casino operator must submit a notification to the Authority within 14 days of the decision, setting out the details of its decision (including its reasons).
(3) Without affecting paragraphs (1) and (2), a casino operator must notify the Authority of such matters, in such manner and within such time as the Authority may specify (by prior written notice to the casino operator) upon the casino operator becoming aware of a change occurring in —
(a)any particulars of a vendor submitted in a notice previously given under Part II or III of the revoked Regulations or Part 2 of these Regulations; or
(b)any particulars of a vendor’s personnel submitted in a notice previously given under Part II of the revoked Regulations or Part 2 of these Regulations in relation to a Class 1 notifiable contract.
(4) Where the value of a Class 2 notifiable contract subsequently exceeds the prescribed value specified in regulation 7, a casino operator must notify the Authority of such matters, in such manner and within such time as the Authority may specify by prior written notice.
(5) Any casino operator which contravenes paragraph (1), (2), (3) or (4) shall be liable to disciplinary action.
10. Revoke the Casino Control (Casino Contracts) Regulations 2010 (G.N. No. S 62/2010).

FIRST SCHEDULE
Regulation 6 and Second Schedule
Prescribed matters
Matters related to gaming equipment
1. Supply, maintenance, repair or disposal of gaming equipment.
Financial matters
2. Supply of financing or financial services to the casino operator (except where the supply of financing or financial services is wholly provided by one or more banks, finance companies, insurance companies, securities companies or other financial institutions or entities licensed, registered, approved or otherwise regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore).
3. Supply of debt recovery services to the casino operator (except where the supply of debt recovery services is provided by one or more licensees or class licensees within the meaning of section 2(1) of the Debt Collection Act 2022).
Matters related to casino operations and revenue
4. Supply of management agent services for the management of the casino or any part of the casino operations.
5. Supply of consultancy or other services related to gaming.
6. Supply of consultancy or other services related to information technology.
7. Any matter in relation to which the vendor acquires a right to receive income derived from the casino operator’s gaming revenue.
Matters related to casino security and surveillance
8. Supply, maintenance or repair of security equipment.
9. Supply, maintenance or repair of surveillance equipment.
10. Supply of consultancy or other services related to casino security.
11. Supply of consultancy or other services related to surveillance of the casino premises and designated site.

SECOND SCHEDULE
Regulation 8(1)
Part 1
Prescribed classes of notifiable contracts
First column
Second column
Class of contract
Description of contract
1.Class 1
A Class 1 notifiable contract is any contract between a casino operator and a new vendor —
(a)that relates wholly or partly to any matter prescribed in the First Schedule; or
(b)that exceeds the prescribed value specified in regulation 7 and relates wholly or partly to the supply of goods or services for the operations of the casino.
2.Class 2
A Class 2 notifiable contract is any contract between a casino operator and a new vendor that relates wholly or partly to the supply of goods or services for the operations of the casino, but is not a Class 1 notifiable contract.
Part 2
definitions
1. In this Schedule —
“new vendor” —
(a)in relation to a Class 1 notifiable contract, means a vendor whose particulars have not been submitted in any notice previously given by the casino operator to the Authority under —
(i)Part II of the revoked Regulations; or
(ii)Part 2 of these Regulations in relation to a Class 1 notifiable contract; and
(b)in relation to a Class 2 notifiable contract, means a vendor whose particulars have not been submitted in any notice previously given by the casino operator to the Authority under —
(i)Part II or III of the revoked Regulations; or
(ii)Part 2 of these Regulations in relation to a Class 1 notifiable contract or Class 2 notifiable contract.
